manifest_strategy_literal_mirrors.before: Finally, order semistandard S's in a linear extension of shape dominance. The Murphy cell law preserves the corresponding higher-shape filtration. For a fixed S the action on the vectors m_(S,t) modulo higher terms is the ordinary Specht action, since its coefficients do not depend on the left refinement. Thus the successive quotients are the stated Specht modules. Over the generic field, finite-Hecke semisimplicity makes their multiplicities equal to the trivial-character multiplicities under the ρ-row parabolic by induction/restriction adjunction. This is exactly the ordinary number consumed in the higher-level Mackey count.
manifest_strategy_literal_mirrors.after: Finally, order semistandard S in a linear extension of shape dominance. The fixed-first-index Murphy cell law gives quotients C_M(mu), each R-free, so this filtration is R-split. The perfect contravariant permutation form beta(b_d,b_c)=delta_dc*z^length(d) identifies the row module with its star dual. The independent same-shape source50 pairing identifies C_M(mu)^circ with the ordinary Dipper-James Specht P(mu), using finite-free biduality without nondegeneracy of its self-form. Dualize the R-split Murphy filtration and transport it through permutation self-duality to obtain the ordinary Specht filtration with unchanged semistandard multiplicities. The length-decrease standard-basis rule is T_w*T_a=z*T_(w*s_a)+(z-1)*T_w. Over the generic field the resulting ordinary multiplicities are the trivial-character multiplicities used in the higher-level Mackey count.
